It assumes perfect knowledge of the objective function and constraints, allowing for deterministic computation and predictable convergence to the global optimum. However, real-world problems often involve uncertainty and noise, making deterministic approaches less effective in such scenarios.

In contrast, stochastic optimization techniques account for uncertainty by incorporating random elements into the optimization process. These methods use probabilistic models and algorithms that can handle noisy data and explore the search space more effectively. Stochastic approaches often converge to suboptimal solutions but are better suited for complex problems with inherent noise and uncertainty.
